solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Palm-reader perhaps reckoned without a medium

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the first word stands round the others

blocks.note: as in 'I made it ten o'clock', to reckon or calculate
taken as written
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A fortune teller is said to have made predictions without any spiritualist medium present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' looks like a psychic in a palm-reading scene; it is only the size letter. MADE wraps round A and M to give MADAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune tellers at fairs traditionally style themselves 'Madame' something, so the title stands for such a seer by example.

clue.text: One flying before food is eaten by seagull

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: maw is an old and dialect word for a gull, also spelt mew
a.c., ante cibum, is the prescription instruction 'before food'

explanation.surface: A gull swoops down and swallows a bird that was flying just ahead of its meal.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is the pharmacist's abbreviation of Latin ante cibum, seen on medicine labels; it goes in after the M of MAW to give MACAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large parrot, so it is literally a creature that flies.

clue.text: A river, long around north? Weaver

indicators.note: around places the yearning word on both sides of the compass point

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river
to long for something is to ache for it
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about a long river curving round to the north, ending with a question about a weaver.
explanation.walkthrough: ACHE goes round N to make ACHNE, after A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arachne was the mortal weaver who challenged Athena and was turned into a spider.

clue.text: Orca swimming around bow

definitions.note: the answer is a musical direction meaning 'with the bow'

indicators.note: a swimming creature twists and turns, so its letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A killer whale swims about near the bow of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' is a ship's front in the surface; in music arco tells a string player to use the bow again after plucking.
explanation.definitionFit: Arco is the Italian musical instruction for playing strings with the bow rather than plucking.

clue.text: Stop the man overturning focus for prayer in a mosque

definitions.text: focus for prayer in a mosque

indicators.note: in a down entry, overturning turns the joined words upside down so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: to bar is to stop or prevent
the man referred to as him

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop a man from overturning the focal point of prayer in a mosque.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR HIM read backwards gives MIHRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The mihrab is the niche in a mosque wall that marks the direction of Mecca, which worshippers face in prayer.

clue.text: American trading company holds old worker dear

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for an American trader

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the firm wraps round the rest

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation of company
O is the abbreviation for old
a man is a workman or hand
the French word for dear

explanation.surface: An American trading firm keeps on an old employee it is fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: Dear here is French, a convention Mephisto uses freely; the company abbreviation splits to hold everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Comancheros were nineteenth-century traders from New Mexico who bartered with the Comanche and other Plains peoples.

clue.text: Identify inflections of verb tense in error

indicators.note: in tells us the single grammar letter sits inside the slip of the pen

blocks.note: a typo is a typing error
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A grammar exercise: spot the verb forms in a sentence where the tense has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPO takes T inside to give TYPTO, a verb in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: To typto is to conjugate, from the Greek verb typtō, 'I strike', once the standard model verb that schoolboys recited.

clue.text: Police station, at that time formerly a hospital

blocks.note: than is an obsolete spelling of then
taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A building that was once a hospital has now become a police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' marks THAN as an archaic form, not a time clue for the building.
explanation.definitionFit: In British India a thana was a police station, a word borrowed from Hindi.

clue.text: Old town hall snoop, one previously in corporation

indicators.note: in places the Scots number inside the word for the belly

blocks.note: to snoop is to pry
corporation is a jocular word for a big belly, a tum
ane is an old and Scots form of one

explanation.surface: A snoop who once sat on the town corporation pokes around the old town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a town council beside 'town hall'; here it is a paunch, TUM, holding ANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The prytaneum was the public hall of an ancient Greek city, where the sacred hearth fire was kept.

clue.text: Shrub unknown in Thurso?

indicators.note: in places the algebra letter inside the Scottish word for a town

blocks.note: Thurso is a town in the far north of Scotland, and toon is Scots for town; the question mark flags an example
x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A shrub growing in Thurso that no one can identify.
explanation.walkthrough: TOON with Y inside gives TOYON.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyon is the Californian holly, an evergreen shrub with red berries.

clue.text: Rabbit friend brought up after row

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: to row is to oar a boat
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit's friend is brought up to the house after a family row.
explanation.walkthrough: OAR then PAL reversed gives OARLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarlap is a rabbit whose ears stick out sideways like oars, so the word names that kind of rabbit.

clue.text: Important king coming between two Richards?

blocks.note: write the name twice, RICHARD RICHARD, and take the five letters at the join: the tail of one and the head of the other

explanation.surface: A grand king sits between two men named Richard in a line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is not printed: write the name twice, richARD RIchard, and the answer straddles the join, which is why there is a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ard-ri is Irish for high king, the overlord above Ireland's provincial kings.

clue.text: Soup made by Maori in honour of champion Australian

blocks.note: as in a toast, 'to the bride'
a champion is a hero
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A Maori cook makes a soup to celebrate an Australian sporting champion.
explanation.walkthrough: TO, HERO and A give TOHEROA.
explanation.definitionFit: Toheroa is a large New Zealand clam, and the thick green soup made from it is a Maori and Kiwi delicacy.

clue.text: Bad dream about caliph sheltering revolutionary

indicators.note: to shelter someone is to keep them inside, so the ruler's name wraps round the rebel

blocks.note: ca. is circa, about
Umar was the second caliph of Islam
Che Guevara is the crossword's default revolutionary

explanation.surface: A nightmare about a caliph who hides a revolutionary in his palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The caliph is not a generic title but a named ruler, Umar, the second caliph after Muhammad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauchemar is French for nightmare, a word Chambers lists in English use.

clue.text: English composer shortly penning strain for Scots accepted copying of movements

indicators.note: shortly means the composer's name is cut short at its end
to pen something is to shut it in, so the shortened name holds the Scots word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Chopin without his last letter
rax is Scots for stretch or strain
A is the abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: An English composer, writing briefly, takes on a Scottish piece of strain and is accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Scots' marks a dialect word: the strain is a stretching, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Echopraxia is the involuntary imitation of another person's actions, a symptom in some neurological conditions.

clue.text: In my cup I’d drunk something fruity

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: every letter of these words is used

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker admits to having downed a fruity cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In my cup' sounds like a confession of drinking; the four words are themselves the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pycnidium is the flask-shaped spore-bearing body of certain fungi, a fruiting body in botanical terms.

clue.text: Small piece of ground gone over in this plane?

definitions.note: the answer is a class of aircraft

indicators.note: something gone over is turned back on itself, so it reads from right to left

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A pilot wonders whether a tiny patch of ground could be flown over in this aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: S then LOT reversed gives STOL; the question mark nods to how little runway the plane needs.
explanation.definitionFit: STOL stands for short take-off and landing, an aircraft that can use a very small airstrip.

clue.text: Bird repeatedly heard during Land of Hope and Glory?

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by what the sung word sounds like, not how it is written

blocks.clueFragment: during Land of Hope and Glory?
blocks.note: the song's line 'Wider still and wider' sings this word again and again

explanation.surface: Birdsong keeps cropping up during a performance of Land of Hope and Glory.
explanation.walkthrough: Land of Hope and Glory is the patriotic British anthem sung at the Last Night of the Proms; its chorus repeats 'Wider still and wider'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whydah is an African weaverbird whose breeding males grow very long tail feathers.

clue.text: Snake carrying a new disease in Africa

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the serpent holds the other letters

blocks.note: a naga is a cobra or a serpent of Hindu myth
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A snake is found to be carrying a new African disease.
explanation.walkthrough: NAGA takes A and N inside to give NAGANA; 'carrying' works both as infection and as container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagana is a cattle disease of tropical Africa caused by trypanosomes spread by tsetse flies.

clue.text: No chance bishop after resetting accepts ring with gem unfaceted

indicators.note: to reset is to arrange afresh, as a jeweller resets a stone
to accept something is to take it in, so the rearranged letters take in the circle

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A jeweller tells a bishop there is no chance of resetting his ring, whose gem is unfaceted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NO CHANCE and B are rearranged around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem cut en cabochon is polished into a smooth dome instead of being given flat facets.

clue.text: Correct a leg bone

blocks.note: taken as written
a prop is a support, like a leg holding something up
os is Latin and anatomical for bone

explanation.surface: A doctor confirms a diagnosis: correct, it's a leg bone.
explanation.walkthrough: A, PROP and OS give APROPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means fitting or to the point, so a remark that is apropos is appropriate.

clue.text: All tense being upset about anti-tank weapon launcher

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
about means round the outside, so the jumble goes round the military abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
AT is the military abbreviation for anti-tank

explanation.surface: Everyone is tense and upset about an anti-tank weapon launcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weapon launcher' is the whole definition; anti-tank only supplies two letters for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlatl is the Aztec spear-thrower, a notched stick that hurls a dart with extra leverage.

clue.text: Once approach politician to help wildly frenzied person

indicators.note: wildly means the two little words are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: ny is an old spelling of nigh, to approach
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: In days gone by, someone approached their MP to help, and did so wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: NY, MP and a rearrangement of TO HELP give NYMPHOLEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nympholept is someone seized by a frenzy of longing, as if possessed by a nymph.

clue.text: Money accepted? A lot of muddle over money

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes
in a down entry, over means the pair is flipped to read upward

blocks.note: M is the economists' abbreviation for money supply
A is the abbreviation for accepted on a bill
taken as written
muzz is to muddle or befuddle, shortened by a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks if money was accepted, then admits much of it got muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: M and A, then A MUZ read upward, give MAZUMA. The first 'Money' is wordplay; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazuma is American slang for cash, borrowed from Yiddish.

clue.text: Football move round goal with ball?

blocks.note: O is round in shape
the net is the goal
W is the abbreviation for with
a ball is round like O

explanation.surface: A football move that goes round the goal with the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: O, NET, W and O give ONE-TWO.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two is a quick pass and return between teammates to get past a defender.

clue.text: Wheels in eccentric arrangement

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: read across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone's car is set up in an eccentric arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt out in eccenTRIC ARrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is slang for a vehicle, and a tricar is a three-wheeled motor car.

clue.text: Sage Derby ruins Cheshire lying in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle says only each word's central letter or letters are kept

blocks.note: the centre of a five-letter word
the centre of a five-letter word
an eight-letter word has two central letters
the centre of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: A wedge of Sage Derby cheese spoils the Cheshire lying in the middle of the cheeseboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby and Cheshire are both English cheeses, so 'Sage' looks like part of the cheese; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or inspired poet of the Vedas.

clue.text: Finish our running race

indicators.note: running letters are on the move, so they are jumbled

blocks.note: the finish is the end
taken as written

explanation.surface: We finish our running race.
explanation.walkthrough: END then OUR rearranged gives ENDURO.
explanation.definitionFit: An enduro is a long-distance endurance race for motorcycles or cars.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow stone left neglected in Perthshire town

indicators.note: neglected things are left out, so these letters are dropped from the place name

blocks.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit
L is the abbreviation for left
Pitlochry is a Highland town in Perthshire, Scotland

explanation.surface: A neglected stone is left lying in a Perthshire town, gone brownish-yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: PITLOCHRY loses PIT and L to leave OCHRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochry is an adjective from ochre, the earthy pigment whose colour is a dull brownish-yellow.

clue.text: March past left Pride giving out press release

indicators.note: giving something out means letting it go, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
PR is public relations, the press release

explanation.surface: A Pride march goes past, while those on the left issue a press release.
explanation.walkthrough: L then PRIDE without PR gives LIDE. 'March past' reads as a parade; it means the month in times past.
explanation.definitionFit: Lide is an obsolete English name for the month of March, so it is March in a past age.

clue.text: One of three born in Altrincham

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the place name that follows

blocks.note: Altrincham is a town in Cheshire; the letters sit after its first two

explanation.surface: A triplet born in Altrincham.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in alTRINcham.
explanation.definitionFit: A trin is a triplet, one of three children born at a single birth.

clue.text: Excessive consumer? A wife takes ordinary prize endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the reward word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
ux. is the abbreviation of Latin uxor, wife
O is the abbreviation for ordinary
trophy lacking its last letter

explanation.surface: A wife wins an ordinary prize, though she is a heavy consumer.
explanation.walkthrough: A, UX, O and TROPH(y) give AUXOTROPH.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxotroph is a mutant microbe that needs extra nutrients the normal strain can make itself, hence a demanding feeder.

clue.text: So mostly, sirs, I am a bit of an oracle

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

blocks.note: thus without its last letter
MM is messieurs, French for sirs
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone announces, a little pompously, that they are something of an oracle.
explanation.walkthrough: THU(s), MM and I'M give THUMMIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urim and Thummim were objects in the Hebrew high priest's breastplate used to divine God's will, so Thummim is part of an oracle.

clue.text: French composer wrote one bar over without repetition

indicators.note: without says something is removed, and repetition by rote is the thing to take away
over means the rod is turned back to front

blocks.note: wrote with rote, learning by repetition, taken out
I is the Roman numeral one
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A French composer wrote a piece where a bar is played once only, without a repeat sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Rote means learning by repetition, so WROTE without ROTE leaves W; 'bar' and 'repetition' sound like music.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles-Marie Widor was a French organist and composer, famous for his organ Toccata.

clue.text: Short pause — one for energy in argument

indicators.note: one letter for another means it stands in that place instead

blocks.note: a lemma is a premise or proposition in an argument
I is the Roman numeral one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A speaker takes a brief pause, swapping vigour for one more point in the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMMA with I in place of E gives LIMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek prosody a limma is a pause of one time unit, the shortest rest in a line of verse.

clue.text: Little time prying, getting parts separated

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
someone prying is nosy

explanation.surface: A snoop, given a little time to pry, gets the pieces apart.
explanation.walkthrough: MO then NOSY gives MONOSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Monosy is an old botanical term for the abnormal separation of organs that are normally joined together.
